sources.title: Exact C++ ownership and lifetime validation

claims.text: The source requests simplified shared_ptr core logic; the answer explicitly separates its teaching subset from omitted full-library features.
Executable validation confirms the shared control-block reference-count invariant and one-time last-owner destruction across copy, move, reset and large copy fan-out.

validation.command: compile exact C++17 candidate with independent lifetime/assertion harness
validation.reported_stdout: PASS null copy move self-assign reset last-release thousand-copies null-deref destroyed=2
checks: empty owner has null pointer and count 0
copy shares one control block and increments strong count
move transfers ownership without incrementing count
reset isolates new ownership and releases previous ownership exactly once
1000 copies collapse back to one owner without premature destruction
last release destroys managed object exactly once
null dereference follows declared logic_error contract

boundary_tests.expected: copy count increments, move source empties without count increment
old/new managed objects each destroyed exactly once at final owner release
count reaches 1001 then returns to 1 with object still alive

findings: The candidate narrows “simplified shared_ptr” instead of pretending to implement the full standard-library type.
A single shared control block maintains the strong-count invariant across copy, move, assignment, reset and destruction.
Copy-and-swap avoids releasing old ownership before safely acquiring new ownership; move operations transfer the token without increasing the count.
The exact C++17 candidate is compiled with warnings-as-errors and independently exercises null ownership, copy/move/self-assignment, reset, 1000-copy fan-out and last-release destruction.
The concurrency and cyclic-reference limitations are explicit, preventing the teaching implementation from being misrepresented as production std::shared_ptr.
